files.description: Bike-share riders, one per row (400 rows): rider_id (six-digit id with leading zeros), display_name (person name, some with accented letters), home_district (one of 6 districts such as "Old Town"), membership (casual, monthly or annual) - these three text columns have inconsistent capital letters and stray spaces; joined_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD; about 2% empty), birth_year (whole number; about 4% empty), credit_balance (two decimals, can be negative; about 5% empty).

task_text: In riders.csv, tidy display_name by removing leading and trailing spaces and writing each word with a capital first letter and the rest lower-case, keeping accented letters as they are. `result` should be the number of distinct tidied names (an integer).
intended_computation: Read riders.csv; tidy display_name (strip surrounding spaces; every word with a capital first letter and the rest lower case; accented letters kept); return the number of distinct tidied names (one integer).

acceptable_variants.notes: a numpy integer is the same count
